profiles.label: Aquatic swimmer — built to travel through water rather than to walk: fins, flippers or a tail drive it and the body is held horizontal. Flippers and paddles count as fins, so having four of them does not make it four-legged — the test is whether it walks about on land on those limbs, and if it cannot, it belongs here. A body that swims with a tail or fluke instead of legs belongs here even if its upper half is human-shaped. An animal that swims well but still walks on four legs ashore is `quadruped`, not this (fish, shark, dolphin, seahorse, ray, mermaid)

Bird — TWO legs only: its wings ARE its forelimbs, feathered, plus a beak. Walks, hops or struts upright on two legs; flies (or, for flightless birds, still stands and walks on two) (sparrow, eagle, owl, chicken, penguin, ostrich)

Humanoid — a person-shaped body: fully UPRIGHT on two legs with the hands free, not used for walking. Strides heel-to-toe with the arms swinging in opposition and the hips counter-rotating, torso stable and vertical. Covers anything built on a human frame, real or invented, including shaggy, ape-like or monstrous ones — fur and a beast's face do not make it a `primate` if it strides upright with its hands free. It must have TWO LEGS that it walks on: a human-headed body with four legs, or with a fish tail instead of legs, is not humanoid — classify those by how they get around (human, alien, superhero, robot, elf, zombie)

Primate — two arms with HANDS plus two legs, torso semi-upright rather than horizontal. Moves on all fours with its hands (or knuckles) in contact with the ground, shoulders rolling with each stride; sits upright, and grips, carries and grooms with its hands. It is NOT fully upright and its hands are used for locomotion — a body that walks fully upright with its hands free is `humanoid`, not this, however ape-like, hairy or beast-like it looks (monkey, ape, gorilla, chimpanzee, orangutan, lemur)

Four-legged land animal — four walking legs and NO wings. Walks, trots and runs on all fours with a diagonal gait; may have a tail. Includes lizards and other four-legged reptiles, and animals that GLIDE on a skin membrane rather than beating wings. Its front limbs are LEGS, not arms with hands (dog, cat, horse, bear, elephant, komodo dragon, flying squirrel)
Limbless slitherer — no legs, no fins, no wings at all. Moves by undulating its whole long body against the ground (snake, python, eel, worm, legless lizard)

Winged flyer — wings IN ADDITION to its legs, not instead of them: either four legs plus a separate pair of wings, or an insect's legs plus wings. Can walk on its legs and fly by beating wings that are not its forelimbs. Gliding on a skin membrane does NOT count — the wings must beat (dragon, wyvern, griffin, bat, butterfly, bee, pegasus)
